focus: Explain entropy in bits from editable nonnegative outcome weights. Normalize weights by a positive total. Let the learner change weights and resize the actual vector from 2 through 6 outcomes, preserving retained values and appending zero. Compare actual H with log2(length(weights)), and explain why appending zero preserves H while changing its possible maximum. Include a positive common scale factor and display its changed scaled weights/total alongside unchanged probabilities and entropy to teach normalization invariance. Do not declare a separate scalar outcome-count control: count comes directly from the vector length. Use vector bar views and scalar computed readouts, no line view. Treat weight normalization and zero-term convention as teaching constructions/derivations. Preserve source-supported formula, certainty and uniform-maximum attribution, with equation-symbol spacing/transcription labels.
excerpt:
A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Section 6, Choice, Uncertainty and Entropy, Theorem 2 and properties 1-2, printed pages 10-11.
Prose excerpt: With equally likely events there is more choice, or uncertainty, when there are more possible events.
Prose excerpt: Thus only when we are certain of the outcome does H vanish. Otherwise H is positive.
Prose excerpt: For a given n, H is a maximum and equal to log n when all the p_i are equal. This is also intuitively the most uncertain situation.
The preceding prose preserves the words of the source, with equation-symbol spacing transcribed for readability.
Equation transcription of Theorem 2 with base-2 units: H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)), where p_i are probabilities and sum(p_i)=1.
Teaching convention derived by continuity: a zero-probability entropy term contributes zero, using the limit of p*log2(p) as p approaches zero, rather than evaluating log2(0).
Teaching input construction: nonnegative numeric weights with positive total are divided by their total to obtain probabilities. This input construction is not quoted from the paper.
